recipes.title: Soothing Ginger & Silken Tofu Rice Congee
recipes.description: A velvety, slow-simmered jasmine rice porridge infused with fresh ginger root, mild white miso, and pasteurized silken tofu cubes. Designed for low-odor preparation and effortless swallowing.

ingredients.rawText: 1 tbsp fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced

instructions: Combine rinsed jasmine rice, vegetable broth, and sliced fresh ginger in a medium pot.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer partially covered for 22–25 minutes, stirring occasionally until the rice breaks down into a creamy porridge.
Whisk the white miso paste with 2 tablespoons of warm broth in a small cup, then stir into the congee along with the cubed silken tofu.
Simmer for 2 full minutes until tofu is thoroughly heated through (165°F/74°C for neutropenic safety).
Allow to cool to a lukewarm temperature before serving to minimize food aroma and soothe oral tissues.
foodSafetyWarnings: Ensure tofu is from a sealed, pasteurized package and heated thoroughly in the simmering broth.
Do not garnish with raw unwashed scallions if following strict neutropenic precautions.
treatmentConsiderations: Serving lukewarm rather than piping hot reduces steam aromas that can trigger chemotherapy-related nausea.
Neutral tofu protein avoids metallic taste reactions common with red meats.
recipes.sourceName: Memorial Sloan Kettering Oncology Nutrition Kitchen

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Provides 350ml+ of hydrating broth alongside gentle starch and plant protein.

recipes.title: Golden Butternut Squash & Red Lentil Velouté
recipes.description: A nutrient-dense, pureed soup combining roasted sweet squash and hull-less red lentils with a touch of coconut milk and ginger. Rich in plant iron and beta-carotene with zero chewing required.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup split red lentils, rinsed thoroughly
3 cups low-sodium vegetable or bone broth

instructions: Wash and peel the butternut squash thoroughly on a clean cutting board.
In a soup pot, combine the squash, rinsed red lentils, broth, and fresh ginger. Bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer for 18–20 minutes until both squash and lentils are completely tender.
Stir in the canned coconut milk and olive oil, then blend until completely velvety using an immersion blender.
Serve warm in small mugs for easy sipping throughout the afternoon.
foodSafetyWarnings: Wash whole squash under running water before peeling to prevent surface bacteria transfer.
Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and consume within 48 hours after reheating to a rolling boil.
treatmentConsiderations: Formulated without garlic, onion, or black pepper for patients experiencing mouth sores (mucositis) or odor aversions.
Can be sipped from a mug when utensils feel tiring.
recipes.sourceName: National Cancer Institute — Eating Hints Collection

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Split red lentils dissolve completely when cooked, preventing fibrous texture irritation.

recipes.title: Cool Peach & Pasteurized Greek Yogurt Protein Whip
recipes.description: A chilled, odor-free high-protein blend made with peeled cooked or canned peaches, pasteurized Greek yogurt, oat milk, and a hint of maple syrup. Ideal when warm food smells trigger nausea.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup canned or peeled stewed peaches in juice

instructions: Ensure blender pitcher and blades have been washed in hot soapy water or dishwasher cycle.
Add pasteurized Greek yogurt, peaches, oat milk, rolled oats, and maple syrup to the blender.
Blend on high for 45 seconds until completely smooth and airy.
Serve chilled in a covered tumbler with a straw to further reduce food scent exposure.
foodSafetyWarnings: Use commercially canned peaches or thoroughly cooked peeled peaches during neutropenic phases.
Verify Greek yogurt is pasteurized and avoid raw unpasteurized honey.
treatmentConsiderations: Chilled foods emit minimal volatile aroma compounds, making them far easier to tolerate during nausea peaks.
Mildly tart-sweet fruit flavor helps mask persistent bitter or metallic taste sensations.

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Concentrated protein in a compact 1-cup serving for early satiety.

recipes.title: Poached Herb Chicken & Sweet Potato Mash Bowl
recipes.description: Tender chicken breast poached gently in bone broth and served over whipped sweet potato with olive oil. High protein density with extra broth drizzle to support dry mouth.

ingredients.rawText: 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
1 tsp dried thyme or parsley (cooked with broth)

instructions: Place peeled sweet potato cubes in a pot of water, bring to a boil, and cook for 15 minutes until fork-tender.
In a separate saucepan, submerge chicken breast in chicken bone broth with dried herbs. Simmer gently until internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) on a food thermometer.
Shred the poached chicken finely using two forks and moisten generously with 1/2 cup of the warm cooking broth.
Mash the drained sweet potato with olive oil and a splash of warm broth until pillowy and smooth.
foodSafetyWarnings: Always verify poultry reaches 165°F (74°C) using a clean digital thermometer.
Use separate cutting boards for raw poultry and cooked foods; add herbs during cooking rather than raw at the end.
treatmentConsiderations: Finely shredding poultry and serving in warm broth prevents dryness that can make swallowing difficult.

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Lean complete amino acid profile paired with easily digested complex carbohydrates.

recipes.title: Warm Cinnamon Stewed Apple & Oat Compote
recipes.description: Peeled apples simmered until cloud-soft with rolled oats, maple syrup, and gentle Ceylon cinnamon. A comforting breakfast or evening snack rich in soluble fiber.

ingredients.rawText: 2 medium apples, peeled, cored, and finely diced

instructions: Wash apples thoroughly, then peel and core completely.
Simmer diced apples in water with cinnamon for 6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in rolled oats and maple syrup; cook for another 5–6 minutes until creamy.
Serve lukewarm.
foodSafetyWarnings: Peeling fruit and cooking thoroughly eliminates surface microbial risk for immunocompromised patients.
treatmentConsiderations: Cooked apple pectin and soluble oat fiber help regulate bowel comfort gently.

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Low fat content allows rapid gastric emptying when nausea is present.

recipes.title: Zesty Garlic Tomato Chickpea Stew
recipes.description: A hearty Mediterranean chickpea stew simmered in crushed tomatoes, garlic, onion, and red pepper flakes. Rich in fiber and plant protein for days when appetite and spice tolerance are strong.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 tsp chili oil or red pepper flakes

instructions: Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, chickpeas, and chili oil; bring to a lively simmer for 20 minutes.
Mash half of the chickpeas slightly to thicken the broth and serve warm.
foodSafetyWarnings: Wash top of canned goods before opening and simmer thoroughly.
treatmentConsiderations: Contains acidic tomatoes, garlic, and chili spice — avoid during active mouth sores (mucositis) or acute nausea.

nutritionHighlight.gentleDigestibilityNote: Best suited for recovery phases without active mucosal irritation or garlic sensitivity.
